title: WTF Happened to Blockbuster?
description:
In 2004 Blockbuster had around nine thousand stores. Today there is one. Here's how the king of movie rentals lost everything.

(TEST VIDEO: numbers are rounded; verify before publishing.)

scenes.heading: The King
scenes.text: In 2004, Blockbuster was everywhere. It had around nine thousand stores, and Friday night meant one thing for millions of families: a trip to pick up a movie.
But a big part of its profit came from something customers hated. Late fees. Return a movie a day late, and you paid for it.

scenes.heading: The Mistake
scenes.text: In 2000, a tiny startup called Netflix offered to sell itself to Blockbuster for fifty million dollars. Blockbuster's leadership reportedly turned the offer down.
Netflix mailed DVDs with no late fees, then moved to streaming. Blockbuster was slow to follow, and its stores started to disappear.

scenes.heading: The Lesson
scenes.text: In 2010, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy. Today, just one store remains, in Bend, Oregon. The lesson? The business that is winning today can be the one that refuses to change tomorrow.
